_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel set another all-time record at $6.529/gal for the week of 9/21 — keep billing the full fuel surcharge, and don't trim it on early pullback chatter until the next print confirms. Dry van is finally showing $3.01/mi all-in and Yakima-to-Northeast reefer is paying $11.7k-$13.7k a load, so counter harder on both — linehaul is flat and fuel's doing the lifting, so protect your base rate.

_sourcing.status: FOURTEENTH straight cycle with WebFetch/curl egress blocked (eia.gov WebFetch = EGRESS_BLOCKED; curl = CONNECT tunnel 403). WebSearch only. asOf advanced to 2026-09-21 (EIA diesel week; DAT wk ending 9/19; USDA wk ended 9/22 all reflect roughly this window). A 9/28 EIA print ($6.382, down) exists in one source but is unconfirmed and contradicted by FreightWaves — NOT used, asOf deliberately not advanced to 9/28.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE. $6.529/gal for EIA week ending 2026-09-21, up $0.244 w/w from $6.285 (arithmetic checks) — third straight all-time record week, highest in EIA records back to 2007. Sources: weeklydiesel.com (DOE tracker, 'week of September 21, 2026'), DAT Truckload Market Report via AJOT (cites EIA $6.529 for week ending 9/21), IndexBox EIA weekly update 9/22. UNRESOLVED 9/28 reading: IndexBox reports EIA $6.382 for 9/28 (down $0.147 w/w; arithmetic checks) but that is a single source, while FreightWaves ('Diesel Up 10 Cents, Spot Rates Up 2: Margin Squeeze') says diesel rose $0.10 to just under $6.57 as of 9/28 — a different, unreconciled series (6.57-0.10 does not equal EIA's 6.529). Direction of the 9/28 print is therefore unconfirmed, so trend stays 'up' and the number stays at the verified 9/21 record. If the EIA $6.382 dip is confirmed next cycle, flip trend to 'flat'/'down' and note Hormuz premium easing.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: CARRIED FORWARD (aging). $3.42/mi, FreightWaves SONAR NTI 7-day avg dated 2026-09-16. FreightWaves' ~9/28 piece says spot rose only $0.02 w/w and NTI is 5.2% above $3.28 a month ago (implies ~$3.45) but gives no absolute figure, so not promoted (derived numbers are not fabricated in). Needs a clean absolute dated NTI reading.
_sourcing.modality: Dry Van PROMOTED to $3.01/mi ALL-IN — DAT week Sept 13-19, 2026 (AJOT headline 'Van spot rate climbs 5 cents to $3.01 as diesel rises 32 cents'); linehaul $2.17 held flat, fuel surcharge accounted for the entire increase. Arithmetic checks (2.17 linehaul + ~0.84 FSC at $6.285 diesel). Note the prior week's van all-in was $2.96 (+4c, diesel +37c week) — one search summary conflated the two; $3.01 is the Sept 13-19 figure. First clean all-in dry van reading in many cycles. Dry van yoy +32-33% is DAT LINEHAUL yoy (week 9/13-19 report cites van +32%, reefer +36%, flatbed +28%; prior week 33/38/29) — not all-in yoy. Reefer $3.59 UNCHANGED but AGE-FLAG: the $3.59 (+9c, 'diesel jumps 37 cents') arithmetic matches the DAT week using the 9/7 diesel print (week ~Sept 6-12), not 9/19 as previous cycle dated it; no clean newer reefer all-in found for 9/13-19. Reefer/flatbed LINEHAUL eased slightly week 9/13-19 (fuel masked it) — first faint softening sign under the surface, not yet visible in all-in. Flatbed range $3.46-$3.57 carried ($3.55 all-in was reported for the Sept 6-12 week, inside the range); yoy updated to +28-29% (DAT linehaul). LTL and Intermodal unchanged, no new data.
_sourcing.commodityRates: General Dry Freight PROMOTED 2.47 -> 3.01 (tracks dry van all-in, same convention as reefer). Frozen Seafood/Poultry and Fresh Produce 3.59 (reefer all-in; age-flagged as above). Coiled Steel 3.57 and High-Value Electronics 2.60 carried forward unchanged.
_sourcing.lanes: Yakima, WA -> Northeast (reefer) REFRESHED LIVE at $11.7k-$13.7k/load — USDA AMS refrigerated truck rates, week ended 2026-09-22, via IndexBox summary of agtransport.usda.gov rows: Baltimore midpoint $11,700, Boston $13,650 (New York $12,950, Philadelphia $11,500; Yakima->Miami $14,150). Up from $9.9k-$10.8k (wk ended 9/15). DAT reefer blog headlines corroborate direction (Yakima apples topping $14K into the East). Atlanta -> Miami: CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged — only generic broker/blog ranges surfaced (reefer $2.20-3.00, off-season), no clean dated absolute. Memphis -> Atlanta: not searched, unchanged.
_sourcing.blurb: Rewritten around the record diesel print (bill the full surcharge; do not cut on unconfirmed pullback), dry van's promotion to $3.01 all-in, and the Yakima lane jump; coaching is hold base linehaul because fuel, not freight, is lifting all-in rates.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: (1) EIA 9/28 diesel: $6.382 down (IndexBox, single source) vs ~$6.57 up (FreightWaves) — needs primary EIA confirmation. (2) spotAllIn is 13 days old. (3) Reefer $3.59 possibly a week older than labeled. (4) Atlanta->Miami still needs a clean dated absolute $/mi; try AMS Southeast district report. (5) Reefer season winding down in the Southeast/California; Yakima still peaking — watch reefer linehaul next cycle.
